source_text.GH#2699: SECURITY prio 1, PR 2 of #2697: aggregate route migrates to the shared restricted-field walker; join clause closed.

task.description: WF-02 step 3b test-design validation for GH #2699. Static review only; mix was not run.

result.summary: PASS (static; nothing executed, hosted CI is the first run). Every design test A-1..A-10b, A-12..A-16 is present, runnable, with no @tag :skip and no TODO. Fixtures copy the walker test's already-validated tenant, definition and promotion helpers, and each test provisions its own tenant, so they are isolated. No secrets. Verified against router code: parse_aggregates, parse_group_by and parse_join_clause all return {:query_field_invalid, _}, which renders 400, in build_aggregate_request before the guard, so the A-10b 400 expectations hold. A JSON array body arrives as %{"_json" => _}, object_body returns :malformed_json, and the 400 detail is exactly 'request body must be a JSON object'. A no_such_fk join goes through resolve_named_relation to a 4xx, so the ordering test (4xx, not 403, bodies equal) is sound. A-14 strictness is not too strict: Error.forbidden carries no instance or path, the type URL is problems_base + 'forbidden', and the trace id is pinned, so 'answer_option' cannot legitimately appear in any of the five bodies, including the export one whose path contains it. A-8 not_found carries a fixed detail with no type echo, and the pinned x-trace-id plus Plug.Test add no date or request-id header, so the sorted-headers comparison needs no masking. No wall-clock or query-count dependence. The A-12 source assertions use code lines only: function_code strips # lines, and the \s regexes tolerate CRLF. The T-26 'bare' status 200 line re-uses a body already asserted 200. MUTANT ANALYSIS (static): M1 killed by EntRJ A-1/A-9, A-2, A-3, A-6 and W A-12. M2 killed by the W A-12 deleted-name refutes. M3 killed by W A-12 'exempt?: false'. M4 killed by A-6 (b) and (d), which expect 200 when the restriction sits on the non-owner side, plus A-2. M5 killed by the A-3/A-9 far-hop-only test and A-6 (c). M6 killed only in its binding and catch-all forms by the W A-12 regexes; see gap G1. M7 killed by A-10b. M8 killed by A-8 (through and direct join on a ghost primary, filtered variant). M9 killed by assert_refused detail equality and leak refutes, and by A-14. M10 see gap G2. Mutant counts were not measured: no mix run was permitted, so the TEST-DESIGNER 'reported' counts are not repeated here.
advisory_gaps: G1 (low): M6 variant 'extra else clause {:error, :request_clause_unwalked} -> continue/422' survives the A-12 regexes (only a catch-all or a non-{:ok,_} binding is refuted). Cheap hardening: assert the else block of run_query_aggregate contains exactly one '->'. Router-level HTTP cannot reach :request_clause_unwalked, as the design states.

G2 (low, near-equivalent): M10 'restore redaction on aggregate values' is killed by A-15 only if the mutant changes the envelope shape or crashes. A-15 groups by an unrestricted field, so a set-keyed redaction that touches nothing is unobservable. The design accepts this because no restricted value can reach the response.
G3 (info): the A-1 oracle proof (3 unjoined vs 2 joined) and every 200 twin depend on promote_and_create_table! DDL and a nullable uuid fk, which only hosted CI can confirm.
